correctness.rationale: One-sided endpoint traces agree with the endpoint values of the BV representation by jumps against Df. Positivity bounds each jump response Q_s between zero and one, and the triangle inequality bounds every ratio by the supremum of the jump errors; a single jump gives the reverse inequality. Integrating the Bernstein polynomials and converting beta integrals to binomial tails yields the stated absolute moment: the admissible k lie between B+1 and A-1, with the exceptional k=n counted exactly on A=n+1. The polynomial endpoint values 1/(n+1) are limits of interior-jump errors, not errors of constant endpoint jumps. Independently, pair n-1 Bernoulli(s) trials in A with those in B. Their differences sum to a symmetric integer Z, with each summand taking ±1 with probability q=s(1-s) each. The two unpaired trials minus one contribute zero with probability 2q. The mean absolute moment is E|Z|+(1-2q)Pr(Z=0), giving the three stated small-degree polynomials. Their strict deficits at every interior s integrate to a positive deficit against any nonzero variation measure, proving nonattainment. At the midpoint the absolute deviation of Bin(2n,1/2) telescopes to n choose(2n,n)/4^n; its successive ratio is (2n+1)/(2n) and it crosses 1 from 15/16 to 35/32 between degrees three and four. Thus an interior jump attains the norm for every n≥4. The triangular-array CLT has a bounded-summand Lindeberg condition for any interior parameter limit, and bounded second moments yield convergence of absolute moments. For endpoint parameter limits the second moment after scaling tends to zero. Compactness then gives uniform convergence to 2 sqrt(s(1-s)/pi), with unique maximum at 1/2. This proves the constant and localization for every choice of maximizer, not the finite-degree maximizing location. Direct independent evaluation at n=2, s=1/3 also gives 61/243 on both sides.

value.rationale: The trace convention is standard for the endpoint-interpolating operator, but interior variation does not charge endpoint jumps. This creates a substantive low-degree distinction between a sharp supremum and an actual norming input. The exact binomial representation settles the threshold at degree four and gives a useful prescription and sharp asymptotic comparison for integrated approximation of discontinuous BV inputs.
